Peeking in CS2

Peeking Fundamentals

Peeking is a fundamental technique in CS2 where you expose yourself from cover to gather information or engage in combat.

Key Principle: Always have a purpose when peeking. Whether it's gathering information, taking a duel, or creating space for your team.

Basic Peeking Techniques Comparison

Technique Best Used For Risk Level Effectiveness vs AWP
Wide Peek Aggressive plays, surprising enemies High Good (if timed right)
Short Peek Information gathering Low Excellent
Jiggle Peek Baiting shots, pre-firing Medium Very Good
Common Mistake: Don't re-peek the same angle immediately after getting shot at. The enemy will be ready for you!

Playing Against AWP

DO

  • Use utility before peeking
  • Coordinate with teammates
  • Mix up your timing
  • Use shoulder peeks to bait shots

DON'T

  • Dry peek common AWP angles
  • Re-peek after missing your shot
  • Peek while running (unless executing a specific strategy)
  • Peek without teammate support

Famous Peeking Techniques

XANTARES Peek

An aggressive wide peek with perfect counter-strafing, named after the Turkish player XANTARES.

Execution Wide strafe + instant counter-strafe + shoot
Timing Very fast, almost instant
Difficulty Very High

Ferrari Peek

Maximum speed peek with pre-fire, designed to catch enemies off-guard.

Execution Run peek + pre-fire + counter-strafe
Timing Very aggressive, no delay
Difficulty High

Pre-firing and Re-peeking

Concept Description When to Use Tips
Pre-firing Shooting at a common position before seeing the enemy When enemy position is known or highly likely Learn common angles, practice timing
Re-peeking Peeking the same angle multiple times After using utility or changing timing Change height/angle slightly each time

Movement in CS2

Movement Mechanics

Mastering movement in CS2 is crucial for survival and effective combat.

Key Principle: Good movement makes you harder to hit while maintaining accuracy.

Basic Movement Techniques

Technique Description Key Binds Difficulty
Counter-strafing Stopping instantly by pressing opposite movement key A/D or W/S Medium
Bunny hop Maintaining momentum through consecutive jumps Space + Strafe High
Air-strafing Controlling movement in air Mouse + A/D High
Remember: Moving while shooting drastically reduces accuracy. Always counter-strafe before shooting!

Advanced Movement Concepts

Silent Landing

Landing without making sound by using crouch.

Execution Hold crouch before landing
Use Case Sneaking behind enemy lines
Fall Height Works up to medium heights

Run Boosting

Boosting teammate by running into them while they jump.

Execution Coordinate jump + forward movement
Use Case Reaching unexpected positions
Players Needed 2 players minimum

Movement Speed Comparison

State Speed (units/s) Sound Level Usage
Running 250 Loud Fast rotations, rushing
Walking 130 Silent Sneaking, precise positioning
Crouching 85 Silent Sneaking, accuracy

Sound System in CS2

Understanding Sound Mechanics

Sound is a crucial information source in CS2, often determining the outcome of rounds.

Key Principle: Every action creates a unique sound that can be used to gain information.

Sound Categories

Type Examples Range Information Provided
Movement Steps, jumps, lands Long Position, direction, player count
Weapons Shots, reloads, scopes Very Long Weapon type, position, ammo status
Utility Pins, bounces, explosions Medium Utility type, timing

Sound-Making Actions

  • Running/Walking
  • Jumping/Landing
  • Weapon switching
  • Reloading
  • Scope zooming
  • Utility usage

Silent Actions

  • Walking with Shift
  • Crouched landing
  • Standing still
  • Looking around
  • Walking on crouch

Sound Masking Techniques

Flash Bang Timing

Using flash explosion to mask movement sounds.

Duration ~1 second of sound cover
Best Used For Position changes, rushes

Fake Steps

Creating misleading sound cues to deceive enemies.

Execution Jump + silent land in different direction
Effectiveness High in clutch situations

Utility Usage

Essential Utility Knowledge

Proper utility usage can turn the tide of any round and is crucial for both execution and defense.

Key Principle: Always have a purpose for your utility and communicate usage with your team.

Utility Mastery Progress

Basic Smokes
Essential for all players
Pop Flashes
Advanced technique
Molotov Lineups
Site specific

Utility Decision Tree

Round Start
T Side
  • Map control smokes
  • Info flashes
  • Save HE for execute
CT Side
  • Counter-flash positions
  • One-way smokes
  • Delay molotovs

Advanced Utility Combinations

Site Execute

1. Flash over for info

2. Smoke key angles

3. Molotov common spots

Site Hold

1. Counter-flash rushes

2. Smoke choke points

3. Molotov entry paths

Retake

1. Flash site

2. Clear with HE

3. Smoke plant spot

Types of Utility

Type Cost Primary Use Advanced Uses
Smoke $300 Block vision One-ways, fake executes, rotations
Flash $200 Blind enemies Pop flashes, sound masking
HE Grenade $300 Damage Wallbang damage, finish low HP
Molotov/Incendiary $400/$600 Area denial Post-plant, force movement

Pop Flash Techniques

Flashes that give enemies minimal time to react.

Self Pop Flash Right-click throw while turning away
Team Pop Flash Coordinate timing with peek

Smoke Lineups

Consistent ways to smoke off key positions.

Jump Throw Bind "jump" + "throw" for consistency
Run Throw Use specific positions and timings
Common Mistakes: Don't waste utility early in the round without purpose, and always save some utility for late-round situations.

Position Playing

Understanding Positions

Position selection and playing style can make the difference between winning and losing rounds.

Early Round (0:00 - 0:20)

T Side
  • Default spread
  • Map control positions
  • Info gathering spots
CT Side
  • Default setup
  • Aggressive peek positions
  • Utility usage spots

Mid Round (0:20 - 1:00)

T Side
  • Execute positions
  • Lurk spots
  • Trade positions
CT Side
  • Rotation positions
  • Crossfire setups
  • Info positions

Late Round (1:00+)

T Side
  • Post-plant positions
  • Crossfire setups
  • Time management spots
CT Side
  • Retake positions
  • Flank coverage
  • Kit recovery spots

Position Risk Assessment

Off-Angle
High risk, high reward. Best used sparingly and with team support.
Default
Safe but predictable. Good for consistent play and team coordination.
Aggressive
Very high risk. Only use with proper utility and team support.

CT Positioning

  • Play for information
  • Set up crossfires
  • Have utility ready
  • Position for rotates
  • Use off-angles sparingly

T Positioning

  • Trade positioning
  • Map control positions
  • Post-plant positions
  • Entry paths
  • Lurk positions
Remember: Don't overuse the same positions - good players will pre-aim common spots.

Economy Management

Economy Basics

Understanding and managing team economy is crucial for maintaining momentum and maximizing round win potential.

Buy Decision Flow

Check Team Money

Evaluate all players' funds

Consider Loss Bonus

Factor in consecutive losses

Assess Enemy Economy

Predict opponent's buy

Make Team Decision

Full buy, force, or save

Common Buy Scenarios

First Round (Pistol)
T Side
  • Armor + Utility
  • Tec-9 + Utility
  • Full Utility
CT Side
  • Armor + Kit
  • Five-Seven + Utility
  • Kit + Utility
Force Buy Scenarios
After Pistol Loss
  • Deagle + Armor
  • SMG + Light Utility
Mid-Game Force
  • Galil/Famas + Utility
  • Scout + Armor

Equipment Value Guide

Full Buy
$5,000+
Rifle, armor, full utility, kit (CT)
Force Buy
$2,500-3,500
SMG/cheap rifle, partial utility
Eco
$0-1,500
Save money, minimal investment
Important: Always save enough money for the next round if possible. Don't force buy alone!
